_readme: Trust-on-first-use pins for every binary that ships inside the signed .dmg. The fetch scripts verify a download against this file and REFUSE to install on a mismatch; scripts/verify-sidecars.sh checks what is currently installed and runs as part of the release gate. Moving a pin requires re-running the fetch script with --accept-new, which rewrites this file - and the resulting git diff IS the human review step. That is the whole point: an upstream swap becomes a visible change to a committed file instead of a silent one on the network. Publisher checksums are cross-checked where they exist, but they are served by the same host as the artifact, so this file is the only anchor a compromised publisher cannot move. kind=source pins bytes we built ourselves: a changed hash there means a rebuild, not an attack, but it should still be a deliberate diff.

yt-dlp.publisher_checksums: SHA2-256SUMS on the same immutable release
